comments.body: that issue was not introduced in #1822, but the issue is real. and the same issue is most probably reproducible on newer openai models. and so temperature should not be hardcoded

Thanks @frutik, you're right on both counts. I mis-attributed it: the adapter came in with #1802, and the hardcoded `temperature: 0.7` goes back to `LlmService` in #1676. I'll fix the description.

And yes, OpenAI's reasoning models (o-series, gpt-5) only accept the default temperature, so `open_ai.rb` hits the same 400.

Proposal: an optional `llm_temperature` judge option next to `llm_model`/`llm_timeout`, sent by both adapters only when set. That needs no migration. One thing to decide: existing OpenAI judges would move from 0.7 to the model's default (1.0) unless the form pre-fills 0.7 for the OpenAI provider. Which would you prefer? Or would you rather keep this PR to the Anthropic fix and do temperature as a follow-up?

> existing OpenAI judges would move from 0.7 to the model's default 

As far as I can see, the default recommendation for OpenAI is not to touch the temperature setting at all. So the default should be fine, but the final call is up to @epugh

Thanks @frutik. Following that, I pushed c21e5ca: the OpenAI adapter no longer sends `temperature` either, so both adapters use the provider's default. A new test checks the OpenAI request has no `temperature` and fails with the old line restored. The judge tests pass (70 tests) and rubocop is clean. I've updated the description.

@epugh, the one behavior change: existing OpenAI-dialect judges (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama) move from 0.7 to their provider's default. If you'd rather keep 0.7 configurable, I can add an optional `llm_temperature` judge option in a follow-up.

i think temperature is a cool setting from two years ago that most people proprbably don't need to touch...   

Thanks @frutik for reviewing this and approving it!
pushed this to go.quepidapp.com, feel free to confirm the fix!
